A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, algorithms, and central theorems. All 25 pages of v1 and 31 pages of v2, including their appendices and equations, support comparison. Existing proofs can be matched across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical bounds and proofs, including its appendices, but no original experiments, simulations, or empirical data analyses.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical. Its added bandit examples are analytical illustrations, while statements about empirical performance are attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: Both versions analyze the same TAS and S-TAS procedures, including mean projection, C-tracking, total-order answer selection, and stopping rules. Specifying the confidence coefficient more explicitly in v2 does not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts empirical task evaluations. The structured-bandit definitions and epsilon-best-arm example added in v2 are theoretical illustrations, not newly evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison algorithms experimentally. Expanded discussion of TAS variants and Top-Two methods concerns cited research rather than new baseline comparisons.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an empirical evaluation protocol. Changes to analytical confidence thresholds and stopping-time bounds do not establish changes to experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports empirical ablations, robustness tests, or error analyses. The new assumption examples and hard-instance calculations are mathematical analyses assessed under T1 and C2.

E5.justification: Neither reports experimental repetitions, seeds, error bars, or significance tests. Revised concentration inequalities concern theoretical guarantees, not uncertainty reporting for empirical results.

E6.justification: Neither version reports measured performance or numerical experimental results. Revised bound coefficients and new analytical rates are theoretical changes covered by T1.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2 replace soft-order remainders with explicit g(t) formulas, and the concentration argument changes from an implicit D_K and pi^2/24 contribution to 8K and 2eK. New Appendix G adds Propositions 3–4 deriving explicit stopping-time bounds and hard-instance scaling. Appendix A adds structured-model definitions, while Appendix C develops an argument for relaxing the bounded-parameter assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contribution remain first finite-confidence guarantees for TAS and S-TAS, recovering asymptotic optimality. The revised introduction and conclusion emphasize the same single-answer and general multiple-answer scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix C discusses replacing bounded parameters with Lipschitz control, argues applicability to unbounded Gaussian models, and contrasts Bernoulli behavior. Appendix G interprets the bounds in both small-delta and hard-instance regimes. The conclusion newly identifies infinite-answer problems as a setting to which the analysis does not straightforwardly extend.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the confidence/exploration calibration as 8K log(t), whereas v1 specifies D_K implicitly. It also adds a reproducibility statement directing readers to assumptions and complete proofs. These refine documentation of the existing algorithms and analysis.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands comparison with prior research: computational and reported empirical tradeoffs of TAS variants, assumption-by-assumption comparisons in Appendix C, and moderate-confidence and infinite-answer literature in the conclusion. Added references include Simchowitz et al., Al Marjani et al., Poiani et al. (2025), and Osogami et al.; the original novelty positioning remains.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the exposition remain intact. v2 edits the introduction and conclusion, divides related work by answer type, adds appendix sections and a reproducibility statement, and changes numerical citations to author-year citations.

P2.justification: v2 adopts an ICLR layout with a running conference header, revised title and author block, small-cap headings, and reformatted references and contents. Equations and paragraphs reflow, but the single-column presentation remains. Neither version contains figures or data tables.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful assumption and limitation discussions and attempts to make v1's implicit bounds explicit. However, new Appendix G contains unresolved inconsistencies: Proposition 4's coefficient A1 depends on an unspecified t, and footnote 22 applies Young's inequality with exponents below 1 despite Lemma 6 requiring exponents above 1. These affect the principal new theoretical addition, making the net balance between improved explanation and mathematical reliability uncertain.
